name: Electron gun
description: An electron gun: the hot cathode (left) gives at most 0.2 per unit length of its face (its temperature limits it: a stronger field pulls no more), the anode's slit lets a thin beam through, and the small collector on the right should catch it. But the beam's electrons repel one another: it spreads and misses. Place two plates beside the beam to focus it, so that at least 0.24 reaches the collector (averaged over $t = 20$ to $40$). A plate at a lower potential than the beam's surroundings pushes the electrons back toward the axis; too low, and it throws them back.

reality.represents: An electron gun with a temperature-limited cathode

remarks.detail: The cathode gives at most 0.2 per unit length of its face, as a real hot cathode gives at most its Richardson current: a stronger field pulls no more.

remarks.line: A beam spread by its own charge
remarks.detail: The beam's electrons repel one another and it spreads; two plates at a lower potential make a lens that refocuses it.

remarks.line: A sheet beam through a slit
remarks.detail: Infinitely long electrodes make a flat ribbon of a beam; a real gun makes a round beam through a round aperture.

The tube is the same all along its length: its electrodes are long prisms, its electrons long lines of charge, its currents per unit length. A real tube is a few centimetres long and has end effects; the textbooks' planar and coaxial laws assume this symmetry too.
